note: Two kinds of reference, and the difference is the whole point. A CARD is an illustration: a brief you can only judge by eye, so a critic looking at one can be talked into anything. A KIT is a real LEGO set authored in LDraw: it has a part list, a colour count, a submodel tree and a bounding box, so a critic can put ours next to it and lose. Build toward the cards; be judged against the kits.

layers.site: a flat rock plateau with a path in
layers.structure: curtain wall on four sides, four round corner towers, a central keep
layers.skin: grey stone courses, slate conical roofs, battlements along every wall head
layers.services: gatehouse arch, arrow slits, wall walks, stairs
layers.stuff: shrubs at the foot, banners, the garrison

layers.site: a waterfall over layered rock, trees crowding the banks
layers.structure: the stone core chimney and the cantilever slabs it carries
layers.skin: smooth pale concrete terraces, glazing between
layers.services: the stair to the water, the window bands
layers.spacePlan: living floor over the fall, bedrooms set back
layers.stuff: the trees, the water, the rocks in the stream
